subject: Pricing: context-length profiling & token-volume follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: pricing & context-length profiling — next steps

Hi Sam —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so we can size pricing more accurately: 

Summary of use case (from the demo)
- Primary flows: long-form summarization of user-uploaded docs + conversational QA over multi-document context.
- Expected per-request behavior: user prompt + ~1-3k tokens of source context, completion typically ~500-2k tokens for summaries/answers.
- Target SLO: p95 latency ~1.5s-3s for generative flows; some background batching OK for lower-priority jobs.

What we need from you to finalize an initial pricing model: 
1) Monthly call volumes (or MAU -> avg calls per user) and any seasonality.
2) Sample averages if you have them: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens (we can profile if you share anonymized logs or a small sample file).
3) % of calls that will need extended context (32k vs 8k vs 128k). Even rough splits are helpful.
4) Any budget range or target unit economics (e.g., target $/1M tokens or target monthly spend).

Our proposal for next steps:
- If you can send a small sample (or the CSV you mentioned) we can run a quick context-length profiling run to estimate tokens-by-context-tier and give ballpark cost ranges for 8k/32k/128k variants. Jordan will run the profiling and share a short writeup.
- If preferred, we can also start with conservative assumptions and present 3 pricing scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive).

Attaching the Redwood pricing sheet (high-level) for Q2 so you have reference rates.

Thanks — want to schedule a 30-min follow up next Tue/Wed to review profiling results?

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_pricing_sheet_q2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing & context-length profiling — next steps

Marissa — thanks for the recap. Quick answers from our side (rough numbers):

- MAU: ~120k active users.
- Calls: ~2.5M generative calls / month (mix of on-demand summary and background batch summarization).
- Avg tokens we see today (sampled): avg prompt ~350 tokens, avg completion ~1,200 tokens (summaries are long). So total ~1,550 tokens per call on average.
- Context-length split (ballpark): 8k-equivalent flows ~60%, 32k-equivalent flows ~35%, 128k-equivalent (very infrequent) ~5%.
- Budget: initial monthly budget range $5k- $15k while we pilot. If unit economics work we can expand.

I attached a small CSV with anonymized request-level token counts from last week. Can you run your profiling against that? Also: how do you recommend we think about target $/1M tokens? For us, we want cost per 1M tokens inside our budget ceiling that allows reasonable scale.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Lee
Head of AI Product, Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme_token_samples.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing & context-length profiling — next steps

Thanks Sam — this is perfect and gives us a great starting point. A few quick notes and an initial ballpark of unit economics so you can see how the numbers map to your $5k- $15k pilot budget.

Quick thoughts on the sample you sent:
- Jordan will run a small profiling job to bucket calls by effective context tier (8k/32k/128k) and compute avg prompt/completion tokens per bucket.
- If the CSV contains request-level token counts we can run the exact math; otherwise we’ll sample and estimate based on your averages.

Example unit economics (illustrative):
- Using your avg ~1,550 tokens/call => ~3.875B tokens/month for 2.5M calls.
- If we assume a blended unit price of $20 per 1M tokens => ~ $77,500/month (this is illustrative; final price depends heavily on context mix, batching, and quantization).
- For a pilot-sized spend of $5k- $15k/month, we can target optimizations: batching, prefix caching for repeated docs, and a quantized 8k model for the majority of calls to lower unit costs.

Ballpark price guidance we can work toward (examples for discussion):
- 8k-class model (highly-optimized, quantized): target $6- $15 per 1M tokens (depends on commitment and reserved capacity).
- 32k-class model: target $15- $30 per 1M tokens.
- 128k-class model: $40+ per 1M tokens (specialized infra).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Jordan will run the profiling on the CSV and return a short summary (avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, tokens per call, % by context-tier).
2) We’ll return 3 pricing scenarios mapped to your $5k/$10k/$15k pilot targets and show what throughput and user coverage that buys.
3) Quick follow-up call next Wed to review.

Linking the HubSpot deal for visibility: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-001

Thanks — we’ll get the profiling report to you by tomorrow morning.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: profiling_run_request.md (md)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing & context-length profiling — next steps

Hi Sam — Jordan here. I ran a quick, local profile on the sample CSV you attached and here are the initial findings (high-level):

- Sample size: 2,400 calls from last week (anonymized).
- Measured averages: avg prompt tokens = 360; avg completion tokens = 1,150; avg tokens/call = 1,510.
- Context-tier split (sample): 8k-like = 80%, 32k-like = 18%, 128k-like = 2% (your earlier estimate skewed higher for 32k; sample shows majority fits comfortably within 8k).

Estimated monthly tokens (extrapolated from 2.5M calls):
- Total tokens/month ≈ 3.775B tokens.

Cost examples (simple multiply by $/1M tokens):
- At $10 per 1M tokens => ~$37,750/month.
- At $20 per 1M tokens => ~$75,500/month.

Recommendation for a pilot:
- Use an optimized 8k model for the ~80% of calls to keep costs down, and route larger-context requests to a 32k pool with policy-based fallback.
- Apply prefix/KV caching for frequent documents (can reduce completion tokens significantly for repeated tasks).
- If you’re targeting $5k- $15k/month pilot, we should scope the pilot to a fraction of traffic (e.g., 10% of users) and/or prioritize lower-context flows.

Next ask: can you confirm the desired pilot scope (percent of traffic) and whether we should include background batch summarization in the pilot? Also confirm whether sharing a 7-day rolling log feed is possible — if so we can run a full run and provide a more precise cost model (by context-tier and by endpoint).
